newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank steady, seen down on fund injection.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank steady, seen down on fund injection.

text.p: Interbank rates were mostly unchanged in the morning as liquidity remained ample and demand low, money dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the central Bank Negara was constantly monitoring interbank rates with a view to keeping them down through injection of liquidity.
At 0200 GMT, one-month money was at 7.40/50 percent, three-month money was at 7.50/60 percent and one-week rate was at 6.00/40 percent.

Bank Negara has been keeping interest rates under check through injection of funds, after an abandoned defense of the ringgit through intervention drained six to eight billion ringgit from the system.
It also imposed restrictions on local banks to limit their swap transactions to $2.0 million per overseas customer.

Dealers said this has brought many overseas investors to the market to unload their holdings of Malaysian bonds. "There are a lot of offers for bonds from overseas, but not enough demand," one bonds dealer said.
Interest rate futures were untraded until 0200 GMT, but futures dealers said fresh selling was expected on fears that Bank Negara cannot hold down interbank rates for too long.
"There is no indication that there will be any long-term policy measure to keep interest rates down," said a futures dealer with a Malaysian bank.
